# JIP Quota System

The `QuotaClaim` / `QuotaLimit` CRDs and their projection into the native Kubernetes `ResourceQuota` object `jip-quota`. The QuotaSyncer reconciler that performs the projection is described in [jip-controller](readme.md).

## Default QuotaClaim (initial per namespace)

```
count/pods: 10                              persistentvolumeclaims: 0
requests.cpu: 5         limits.cpu: 10      requests.nvidia.com/gpu: 0
requests.memory: 25Gi   limits.memory: 50Gi requests.storage: 100Gi
services.loadbalancers: 0
count/s3buckets.jetbrains.com: 2            count/gcsbuckets.jetbrains.com: 2
count/postgresqldatabases.jetbrains.com: 1  count/mysqldatabases.jetbrains.com: 1
count/ingresses.networking.k8s.io: 5        count/jobs.batch: 20
count/teamcityprojects.sre.jetbrains.com: 24
count/teamcityprojectfeatures.sre.jetbrains.com: 50
count/teamcitybuildtypes.sre.jetbrains.com: 20
count/teamcityvcsroots.sre.jetbrains.com: 100
count/vaultk8sapproles.jetbrains.com: 1
count/spaceapplications.jetbrains.com: 1
count/awsseses.jetbrains.com: 1
count/githubconnections.sre.jetbrains.com: 2
count/gcpprojects.kro.run: 0
```

## Default QuotaLimit (hard max)

```
count/pods: 50                                persistentvolumeclaims: 5
requests.cpu: 10         limits.cpu: 20       requests.nvidia.com/gpu: 4
requests.memory: 50Gi    limits.memory: 100Gi requests.storage: 1Ti
services.loadbalancers: 0
count/s3buckets.jetbrains.com: 10             count/gcsbuckets.jetbrains.com: 10
count/postgresqldatabases.jetbrains.com: 4    count/mysqldatabases.jetbrains.com: 4
count/ingresses.networking.k8s.io: 10         count/jobs.batch: 50
count/teamcityprojects.sre.jetbrains.com: 24
count/teamcityprojectfeatures.sre.jetbrains.com: 50
count/teamcitybuildtypes.sre.jetbrains.com: 40
count/teamcityvcsroots.sre.jetbrains.com: 150
count/vaultk8sapproles.jetbrains.com: 1
count/spaceapplications.jetbrains.com: 5
count/awsseses.jetbrains.com: 1
count/githubconnections.sre.jetbrains.com: 10
count/gcpprojects.kro.run: 0
```

`services.loadbalancers` and `count/gcpprojects.kro.run` default to 0 in both QuotaClaim and QuotaLimit. Raising either always requires SRE to edit both objects - the owner cannot self-serve, because QuotaSyncer skips a claim key above its limit (see [per-resource validation](#sre-editing-quotas) below), so the enforced value stays 0 no matter what the owner writes into the claim.

**A quota of 0 is also used as a feature gate, not only as a capacity limit.** `count/gcpprojects.kro.run` is 0 in the QuotaClaim and QuotaLimit of all three resource-config profiles (`default`, `kubeflow`, `istio`), which is how GCP project self-service is kept off per namespace: an object count of 0 rejects `GCPProject` CREATE at admission, and raising it to exactly 1 both enables the feature and enforces the one-project-per-namespace rule that the flow requires[^gcpprojects-quota]. Treat a request to raise such a key as an enable/disable decision for the feature rather than a sizing question - see [enable-gcpproject-self-service](../../gcp/projects/how-to/enable-gcpproject-self-service.md) and [gcp/projects/kro-self-service](../../gcp/projects/kro-self-service.md).

## Higher Default Quota on Istio-Enabled Clusters

The Istio sidecar's own requests/limits count against the namespace's JIP quota (see [Istio sidecar resource defaults](../networking/#istio-service-mesh)), so the generic default above left little room for the application's own containers once a sidecar was injected - as few as 2 pods (1 app container + 1 sidecar, both at the old 2000m sidecar limit) could exhaust the default 20-CPU-limit quota. Fix (SRE-6532): the JIP namespace-provisioning ConfigMap (`k8s/jip-controller/templates/configmap.yaml`) gained a new top-level `istio` resource-config template alongside the existing `default`/`kubeflow` ones, with a higher `QuotaClaim`/`QuotaLimit`/`LimitRange` profile[^sre-6532-quota]. It is only rendered on clusters with the `istio-base` component (`{{- if hasKey .Values._vars.components "istio-base" }}`), but selection is **per-namespace, not cluster-wide**: cloud-console sets the `jip.jetbrains.com/namespace-type: istio` annotation only when the user requests Istio for that specific namespace (`Istio: true` on namespace creation, unless the namespace type is `kubeflow`)[^sre-6532-cc]. A namespace created without that flag keeps the generic `default` profile even on an Istio-enabled cluster; the `default` template itself has no istio-related branch:

```
QuotaClaim:  requests.cpu: 10   limits.cpu: 20    requests.memory: 50Gi   limits.memory: 100Gi
QuotaLimit:  requests.cpu: 20   limits.cpu: 40    requests.memory: 80Gi   limits.memory: 200Gi
```

(QuotaLimit memory/CPU roughly doubled vs the generic profile's `requests.cpu 10 / limits.cpu 20 / requests.memory 50Gi / limits.memory 100Gi`; other resource types - buckets, DB counts, TeamCity objects - are unchanged from the generic profile.) The Istio-specific profile also bundles the same default `NetworkPolicy` set (`allow-all-inside-namespace`, `allow-monitoring`, `allow-ingresses`) as the generic one.

## Per-Container Ephemeral Storage Limit (LimitRange, not QuotaClaim/QuotaLimit)

Every namespace also gets a native Kubernetes `LimitRange` object named `default`, created by the same JIP namespace-provisioning resource config as the QuotaClaim/QuotaLimit CRDs but as a separate resource type[^limitrange-example]. Its `Container` limits: `default` request/limit (cpu 50m/200m, memory 150Mi/1Gi, ephemeral-storage 100Mi/1Gi) and `max` ephemeral-storage **5Gi**. This cap is unrelated to the QuotaClaim/QuotaLimit system above and is not visible in `kubectl describe quota` - check it with `kubectl describe ns <namespace>` (shows the "Resource Limits" table) or `kubectl get limitrange default -n <namespace> -o yaml`.

The 5Gi default exists because `emptyDir`/container-writable ephemeral storage is bin-packed onto the node's local disk: a shared nodepool sized for many small pods can't absorb every pod claiming a large ephemeral-storage limit without risking eviction of other tenants' pods on the same node when the node's disk fills up[^sre-a-70-ephemeral]. To raise it, SRE edits the namespace's `LimitRange` directly (there is no owner-facing QuotaClaim equivalent for this field): `kubectl patch limitrange default -n <namespace> --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/limits/0/max/ephemeral-storage","value":"20Gi"}]'`. Only do this for namespaces pinned to a nodepool with enough local disk for the requested value per pod times max pods per node - otherwise a burst of large-ephemeral-storage pods can still starve shared-node disk[^sre-7069].

**Caution - a container's `ephemeral-storage` limit and a PVC-backed volume are different budgets.** The `LimitRange` cap applies to node ephemeral storage (writable layer, logs, `emptyDir`) and does not apply to the size of a PVC, including the PVC created by a generic ephemeral volume (`volumes[].ephemeral.volumeClaimTemplate`). A workload can therefore exceed the cap by mounting a PVC - at the cost of one extra quota-tracked object per pod, which is a contention source in high-churn namespaces (see below). Overflow behaviour also differs: exceeding the container `ephemeral-storage` limit gets the pod evicted by kubelet, while a full PVC returns ENOSPC inside the volume and the pod keeps running.

## Quota Operations

Quota `requests.*` and `limits.*` do not have to match. Set `requests.*` to expected aggregate usage, and keep `limits.*` high enough to leave headroom for rollouts and bursts.[^quota-requests-limits-slack]

Job-spawning workloads consume two quota dimensions at once. Each unit of work becomes a `Job` plus the `Pod`(s) it creates - e.g. ZenML runs one Job per pipeline step. When sizing such a namespace, raise both `count/jobs.batch` and `count/pods` together; sizing only by expected pod count under-provisions jobs.[^zenml-jobs-slack]

**Warning - `backoffLimit` is not necessarily uniform across Job types in the same namespace, so a flat "pods = N x jobs" ratio does not size correctly.** A stuck, non-terminal Job can hold Failed pods up to its own `backoffLimit` before TTL cleanup ever applies - see [Job retry deadlock on pod quota](troubleshooting/job-retry-deadlock-on-pod-quota.md). Verified in `zenml-ai-assistant` (2026-09-01): most Jobs at `backoffLimit: 3`, but 11 eval Jobs at `backoffLimit: 30`[^zenml-backofflimit-slack]. Size `count/pods` headroom from the highest `backoffLimit` actually in use (or fix at the Job-spec level), not from a fixed multiplier of `count/jobs.batch`.

**Usage accounting lives in the same object as the limits.** `jip-quota` holds `spec.hard` (limits, written by jip-controller only when QuotaClaim/QuotaLimit change) and `status.used` (counters, rewritten by the API server on every quota-tracked create and by the quota controller on every delete). A namespace that creates and deletes objects at a high rate therefore contends on a single object regardless of how much headroom the limits have, and clients get sporadic `409 Conflict` - see [ResourceQuota 409 Conflict on parallel creates](troubleshooting/resourcequota-409-conflict-parallel-creates.md). Raising quota values does not affect this; reducing the number of quota-tracked objects per unit of work does.

```bash
# View current usage
kubectl describe quota jip-quota -n my-namespace

# Increase quota (within QuotaLimit)
kubectl edit quotaclaim jip-quota-claim -n my-namespace

# Exceeding QuotaLimit → contact SRE
```

## SRE: Editing Quotas

SRE edits only QuotaLimit. QuotaClaim is managed by namespace owners.

**Warning - `agents-*` (macOS build agent) namespaces do not follow this split.** Their QuotaClaim and QuotaLimit are not created by the JIP namespace-provisioning ConfigMap but rendered from the `cluster` chart, which emits both objects with identical values derived from one `agents_quota` knob. The owner therefore has no headroom to self-serve and every increase is an MR on the cluster values file. See [agent pod sizing and namespace quota](../../services/icri/agent-pod-sizing.md).

Quota is never removed entirely - SRE raises QuotaLimit to fit the requested workload instead. For a request to "remove quota", confirm the target workload size and raise the limit to cover it.[^quota-no-remove]

When user requests quota increase beyond default limits:

1. Increase QuotaLimit: `kubectl patch quotalimit jip-limits -n <namespace> --context=<cluster> --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"<resource>":"<value>"}}'`
2. Notify the owner to raise QuotaClaim themselves (via Cloud Console or `kubectl edit quotaclaim`)

QuotaSyncer will reconcile changes to ResourceQuota after QuotaClaim is updated.

**Validation is per-resource, not per-object.** QuotaSyncer iterates `quotaclaim.spec` key by key; a key above its QuotaLimit is skipped with a `validation failed` Warning event (`<resource>: max resource capacity hitted(value/max)`) while every other key is still written to `jip-quota`[^quotaclaim-validation]. Two consequences: an owner whose claim exceeds the limit on one resource is not blocked on the rest, and a *partial* SRE raise takes effect on its own - once `quotalimit.spec[k] >= quotaclaim.spec[k]`, that key applies at the next resync (<= 300s) with no action from the owner. A claim already sitting above the limit therefore needs no re-submission after the raise.

**Size the raise against deliverable capacity, not against the number requested.** QuotaLimit is an admission ceiling, not a capacity reservation - raising it does not create nodes. Before raising, compute what the namespace's target node pool can actually deliver (`total_max_node_count` x node allocatable) and check the cluster and GCP regional ceilings above it: see [capacity ceilings](../nodes/capacity-ceilings.md). A namespace pinned to one pool by `nodeSelector` cannot exceed that single pool no matter what the quota says.

**Warning - raising a quota past deliverable capacity relocates the failure from one namespace to the whole cluster.** While the quota binds, exhaustion is a clean namespace-scoped `exceeded quota: jip-quota` rejection naming the resource. Once the quota is above what the region can supply, the same workload instead drains the shared GCP regional CPU quota, and scale-up then fails for every namespace in the cluster with a message that names neither the cause nor the tenant responsible - see [autoscaler max size due to GCP quota](../nodes/troubleshooting/autoscaler-max-size-gcp-quota.md). When a request exceeds deliverable capacity, the answer is a capacity conversation with the pool owner, not a larger number.

See [how-to/increase-namespace-quota](how-to/increase-namespace-quota.md) for full procedure.

Kubeflow namespaces have separate quota set with higher GPU (8) and CPU (100).

- [gcp/projects/kro-self-service](../../gcp/projects/kro-self-service.md) - GCP project self-service, gated by the `count/gcpprojects.kro.run` quota
